transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Rivera, thank you for coming back in to see me today. I have some information regarding the pathology results from your biopsy.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it the cancer?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: This is very difficult to tell you, but there was a serious mistake. Your specimen was mislabelled in the lab. The diagnosis of cancer we discussed last week actually belongs to another patient.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for any confusion this has caused. The lab was incredibly busy that day and the labels got switched.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So I don't have it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, you do not have the cancer that was described in that report. However, when we re-ran the correct biopsy, the results showed a different type of growth that is aggressive. It means we have lost several weeks of treatment time because of the mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. You said I was sick, then you said I wasn't, now you say I am again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a lot to take in. The first report was wrong because of the label swap. The second report is the one that is correct for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What does that mean for me? Will I be okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Because of the delay, the stage of the disease has progressed. It changes the prognosis, meaning the long-term outlook is not as favorable as it would have been if we caught it three weeks ago.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Are you saying I might die?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you're feeling scared right now. It is a very frightening thing to hear.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't afford to be sick. I don't have papers. If I'm in the hospital for a long time, will they find me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are focused on your care here. The hospital's priority is your treatment, not your status.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But the mistake happened because you were busy. Does that mean you don't care about people like me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand you're feeling neglected or unimportant because of how this happened. I want you to know we are committed to fixing this. But look, I really have to get to my next clinic patient in a few minutes, so I want to make sure we get a plan in place.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're leaving? I just found out my life changed because of a sticker on a jar.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize this is a huge shock. I am sorry that the system failed here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My family expects me to come home. I don't know what to tell them.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is completely natural to feel overwhelmed by how to share this with them.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens now? Do I just wait?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, we are moving quickly now. I have already coordinated with the oncology team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When do I see them?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You will have a consultation with Dr. Aris tomorrow morning at 9:00 AM.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. I need you to bring the folder of records I'm giving you to that appointment. I will personally call the nurse today to ensure your file is flagged for priority.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will the treatment work?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Dr. Aris will explain the specific options, but we are starting a more aggressive protocol to make up for the lost time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just wanted to know I was healthy.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. It's heartbreaking that this happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did the lab make the mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The pathology department had a failure in their scanning process. It was a systemic error in how they verified the patient names.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And now I'm the one who pays for it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can hear how unfair this feels. It is unfair.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know if I can trust you people anymore.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is a completely valid reaction. You have every right to be angry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What if I can't pay for this new treatment?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We have a social worker who specializes in patient advocacy. I'll have her meet you in the waiting room before you leave today to discuss financial assistance.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to go home.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. We'll get these papers sorted, and then you can head home and prepare for tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tomorrow at nine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That's right. 9:00 AM with Dr. Aris. I'll be the one to make sure the appointment is set.

H.justification: The resident uses rushing language by stating, 'I really have to get to my next clinic patient in a few minutes.'

E.justification: The error is named explicitly and lay language is used, but there are no checks for patient comprehension.

A.justification: While the resident says 'I am sorry,' they dilute accountability by attributing the error to the lab being 'incredibly busy' and 'the system failed.'

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('scared', 'neglected', 'unimportant', 'angry') and engages with the patient's specific concerns regarding immigration status and family.

T.justification: The resident provides a specific next step with a timeline (Dr. Aris, tomorrow at 9:00 AM) and a patient role (bring the folder of records), but does not address how to prevent the error from recurring.
